beats.say: A phone can be lost or stolen. Let us protect it in advance and learn what to do.
First: a screen lock. A six-digit or longer PIN, plus fingerprint or face recognition.

checkpoint.prompt: Is a birth year a good PIN?

options.label: Yes, it is easy to remember
options.feedback: A birth year is easy to find, often right on social media.

options.label: No, I choose a random PIN
options.feedback: Right. Pick a random PIN of at least six digits.

beats.say: Second: backups. If photos and contacts are in the cloud, losing the phone means losing only the device.
Phone lost? Act fast: lock it remotely, tell your organisation at once, wipe it if needed.

scenes.title: Phone lost
scenes.intro: In the evening you left your work phone in a taxi. Act step by step from a colleague's phone.

body.text: Last seen: Narimanov district, 5 minutes ago.

steps.say: The find service shows the phone on the map.

actions.label: Lock and show a message
actions.feedback: Right. Locking takes a minute and keeps strangers out of the phone.

actions.label: Erase now
actions.feedback: Erasing is the last step: afterwards the phone cannot be found on the map. Lock it first.

actions.label: Wait until morning
actions.feedback: Every hour gives a thief more time. Lock the phone now.

body.text: Hello! IT support, how can we help?

actions.label: My work phone is lost, lock my account
actions.feedback: Right. Once support locks your work account, no one can open the mail on the phone.

actions.label: I will tell them tomorrow at work
actions.feedback: Work mail is open on that phone. Telling your organisation at once stops most of the harm.

body.text: A blocked number receives no SMS codes.

steps.say: Now you are in your operator's app.

actions.label: Block
actions.feedback: Right. With the SIM blocked, a thief cannot get SMS codes to recover your accounts.

actions.label: Cancel
actions.feedback: If the SIM stays active, SMS codes keep arriving on the stolen phone.

messages.text: Your lost phone has been found. Sign in to see where it is:

steps.say: Half an hour later, this text arrives.

actions.label: Open the link
actions.feedback: After a theft, texts like this aim to steal the account password, which can unlock the phone.

actions.label: Block and report
actions.feedback: Right. Check the phone's location only in the find service yourself.

scenes.prompt: Your phone is gone. Put the steps in order.

items.label: Lock the phone with the find my phone service
Tell your organisation's technical support at once
Call your mobile operator to block the SIM card
Change important passwords from another device
If it will not be found, erase it remotely

scenes.explain: Lock and report first, then protect the SIM and passwords. Erase last, as an erased phone is harder to find. If your organisation's procedure sets another order, follow it.

body.text: We have logged your lost phone and paused your work account. Come to the office for a new password.

cards.explain: No link or code is asked, you are invited to the office in person. This is the right procedure.

body.text: I found your phone. Write me the screen lock code so I can check you are the owner.

cards.explain: Returning a phone does not need the lock code. Do not give it, arrange the handover through the police.

body.text: Reminder: a new system update for phones is out. Install it from Settings.

cards.explain: There is no link, it sends you to your phone's own Settings. That is exactly where updates are installed.

messages.text: Your cloud storage is full and your photos will be deleted today. Pay here:

cards.explain: A real warning shows up inside the app itself. Do not pay through a link, open the app yourself.

options.label: No lock
options.feedback: Anyone who finds an unlocked phone sees everything.

options.label: Your birth year
options.feedback: A birth year is easy to find, often it is on social media.

options.label: A random PIN of at least six digits
options.feedback: Correct. A long random PIN is hard to guess.

options.label: Fingerprint or face, plus a strong PIN
options.feedback: Correct. It is convenient and the backup PIN is strong too.

scenes.explain: A lock is the first protection when a phone is lost. A fingerprint is handy, but the main PIN must still be strong.

points: A strong screen lock and automatic updates
Turn on backup and find my phone in advance
Phone gone: lock, report, erase if needed
